input.question: Why do my legs get itchy when I run and how can I stop it?
input.ground_truth: It's an allergic reaction. I used to have the same thing happen to me occasionally when I biked a lot (45 miles at a time). The condition, which can be quite severe, is called [exercise induced urticaria](_URL_1_) There are a few theories on how it happen. One is out of shape types' bodies aren't used to the physical activity and the new activity causes capillaries (the tiny blood vessels in your body) to open, stimulating nearby nerves sending an "itch" signal. According to the [wikipedia article](_URL_0_), it can be linked to dietary issues that runners (and others) have, as in they eat certain foods before running and this leads to the allergic reaction during exercise. It can also be caused by hot showers, "fretfulness" (i'm not sure what that means) or fever. Many people find taking an antihistamine before exercise helps (worked for me, after a few weeks it stopped), while others need much more extreme measures. Be careful, in rare cases it can lead to anaphylatic shock.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your legs are like your skin is wearing a cozy sweater that’s a little too tight. When you run, your legs move a lot and get warm. That makes your skin want to scratch because it feels funny or tickly inside the "sweater." 

To help your legs not feel itchy when you run, you can:
- Wear clothes that are not too tight, so your skin can breathe.
- Drink water before and after you run, so your skin stays happy.
- Try not to run too fast at first if you’re new to running—your body needs to get used to it.
- If your legs still feel itchy, you can ask a grown-up to help you pick a special cream that makes your skin feel better.

Your body is just saying, “Hey, I’m working hard!” and sometimes it feels a little funny. But if it keeps happening, it’s good to talk to a grown-up or doctor.
